gen-luckiest-guy-gf-hind-siliguri: Hind Siliguri hums along at a constant line weight, its rounds gapping open like a cracked bangle. Luckiest Guy does the loud shouting, Hind Siliguri the steady, easy talking.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-huninn: Huninn reads crisp and modern, its lowercase climbing close to cap height while its s terminals hold off from the body. Luckiest Guy brings the noise, and Huninn would stay easygoing over pages.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-inter-tight: Loud meets tidy: Luckiest Guy pours out cheerful ink while Inter Tight keeps its ascenders short and its curves tucked in. Mostly it's the gap between a shout and a murmur.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-khula: A ruler-straight shout, then a soft murmur below. Luckiest Guy sets a constant-width line high on the page, and Khula's tall midsection with open-mouthed curves settles in beneath it.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-krub: Krub stands tall, its curves lifting off before the loop closes. Luckiest Guy draws its flat, fineliner-like line loudly, and Krub keeps paragraphs moving at a steady, pleasant pace.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-lexend-deca: Lexend Deca draws a plain line that never swells. Give Luckiest Guy plenty of size and let Lexend Deca stay modest, since its big lowercase carries well beside small-looking capitals.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-liter: Liter reads upright and uniform, with no stroke contrast at all and wide mouths on its round forms. Liter gives the loud, cheerful Luckiest Guy something solid to lean on.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-mada: Luckiest Guy is cheerful and loud, its poured ink and high mean line impossible to miss. Mada, with a towering midzone and curves that refuse to close, reads easily down the page.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-martel-sans: Ink poured in a single width, free of hairlines and shadows, gives Luckiest Guy its loud, cheerful swagger. Martel Sans, with generous openings in every curve, is the quiet foil.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-matangi: Matangi has a hefty lowercase, its strokes like twine pressed flat. Beside Luckiest Guy's cheerful, loud shout, that sturdy body holds its own, so neither font gets pushed around.
